# Let another solver own the loop

[Export a borrowed host field, negotiate an interval and impose new data at the accepted endpoint.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

OpenPFC need not own the outermost time loop. This refactors the external
coupling example into a small host orchestrator that reads a field, chooses
an interval and imposes an endpoint value. It demonstrates the interface
seam; the host is not an implemented finite-element solver.

## Give the session a lifetime and a communicator

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="session" dedent=4}
```

Duplicating a communicator preserves the rank group while creating a
separate message-matching context. The example uses that communicator for
its host reduction. A coupled application must also pass the isolated
communicator into each communicating OpenPFC operation it constructs;
duplication alone cannot redirect an operation that still uses WORLD.
The session and its fields are destroyed before MPI finalizes.

## Borrow, read, impose, commit

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="orchestrate" dedent=4}
```

The host allows 0.25 time units, while OpenPFC proposes 0.1. The clock takes
the smaller limit and clips it again at save boundaries and the final time.
`export_host_field` returns a read-only borrowed view plus geometry. It
neither copies the field nor transfers ownership to the external solver.
This example uses compact, unpadded storage, so its view contains only
owned samples; a padded field requires more careful owned-region handling.
The exported origin is the domain origin. Add `owned_box.low` to local
indices before multiplying by spacing to recover physical coordinates.

The source adapter writes

$$u(x,y,z,t)=\sin x\cos y+0.1t.$$ {#eq-imposed}

```{.cpp include="source.hpp" snippet="source"}
```

It imposes values at the new endpoint; it is not an Euler increment or a
force integrated over the interval. The initial field is zero, so the first
host read is zero; subsequent reads see the last imposed field.

## Start a host-owned experiment

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

The empty input is unused; edit the domain and time constants in C++.
The sibling `source.hpp` is included in the CLI's source snapshot. Two-rank
execution uses `--ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun`. Each rank records the time
negotiation and its complete final field under `results/`.

The checks verify the five clipped intervals, every host read against the
previous accepted state, and all final samples against the imposed formula.
Borrowed handles must not outlive or survive reallocation of their field.
Use the modifier's public field operations for writes so residency tracking
can observe them. A rejected coupled attempt would also need to restore
external solver state; this accept-only orchestrator does not hide that duty.

The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson. It also uses the shared [source.hpp](source.hpp);
keep its relative location when saving the files.

:::
